title:
Comment of Jan Deering in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000, P-15423-000
Submission Date: 11/2/2026

documents.name: 152100.txt
documents.text:
Jan Deering, Eagle River, AK.
I strongly oppose an underwater data center installation in Alaska’s Cook Inlet.  Cook inlet is a regionally important area for Alaskans. It provides a substantial amount of food for South Central Alaskans, myself included. Our subsistence fishing is critical to our annual food supply. Salmon are susceptible to water temperature changes. The residual heat from this development could decimate our salmon population. Salmon returned to the waters they were born in. Once that life cycle is altered, they will never come back. This could affect as much as 60% of Alaskan households. The Cook inlet is also home to protected Beluga whale populations. The noise and heat from this could also aversely affect them. Another location around unpopulated areas with deep water blue water (rather than heavy glacial silt), lower tectonic activity and no subsistence food supply would seem more appropriate. Please keep it away from our people, our wildlife and our food. This is poorly thought out and does not belong in this area.
